packs.name: agent-toolkit
packs.description: A Claude Code marketplace manifest through which one steward's skills, agents, and slash commands are each installed separately.
packs.installs: A Claude Code marketplace manifest at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, registered with /plugin marketplace add and then installed entry by entry with /plugin install <name>@agent-toolkit; each entry names a source directory under dist/plugins/, which scripts/build_plugins.py generates from the repository's skills/, agents/, and commands/ trees. The README also documents npx skills add softaworks/agent-toolkit for Agent Skills hosts and cp -r skills/<name> ~/.claude/skills/ by hand. The README says the skills-installer path also works with Codex, Cursor, and other agents, but documents an install only for Claude Code, so only Claude Code is recorded as a host. This record pins the manifest and does not list, count, or review its entries.
packs.distribution_machinery: scripts/build_plugins.py generates the dist/plugins/ tree the manifest resolves against, and scripts/bump_version.py raises the manifest version. Neither is installed into a host; both operate on the repository's own files.
packs.not_a_system: A marketplace manifest that lists other packs for installation; it is an install source, not a system, and this record never lists, counts, or reviews its entries.
packs.license_note: Repository-wide MIT license file, copyright 2026 Leonardo Flores.

packs.name: Build with Claude
packs.description: A Claude Code marketplace manifest that a host registers as an install source for the plugin packages the repository ships.
packs.installs: The repository's own Claude Code marketplace manifest at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, declaring the marketplace schema and its owner, registered with /plugin marketplace add davepoon/buildwithclaude and then installed entry by entry with /plugin install <name>@buildwithclaude; each entry resolves to a directory under plugins/, and the README also documents copying agent and command Markdown files into ~/.claude/agents/ and ~/.claude/commands/ after a clone. This record pins the manifest and does not list, count, or review its entries.
packs.distribution_machinery: scripts/ holds Node tooling for the repository's own files: validate-all.js and the four per-type validators validate-subagents.js, validate-commands.js, validate-hooks.js, and validate-skills.js against four JSON schemas, generate-registry.js builds the site registry, and fetch-plugins.js with github-search-pagination.js collects external listings. web-ui/ is the project's own website. None of it is installed into a host.
packs.not_a_system: A marketplace manifest that lists other packs for installation; it is an install source, not a system, and this record never lists, counts, or reviews its entries.
packs.license_note: Repository-wide MIT license file, copyright 2025 davepoon.

packs.name: claude-code-tresor
packs.description: A development-workflow kit of skill, agent, subagent, and slash-command documents copied into a Claude Code configuration directory.
packs.installs: 8 SKILL.md skill directories under skills/ in three categories (development, documentation, security), 8 core agent definitions carried both as agents/<name>.md and as subagents/core/<name>/agent.md, 133 agent.md subagent definitions under subagents/ across ten category directories, 24 slash-command directories under commands/ in eight categories, and 6 prompt templates, 11 standards documents, and 10 worked examples under prompts/, standards/, and examples/. scripts/install.sh clones the repository into ~/.claude/tresor and installs from that copy into the host's discovery locations: each skills/<category>/<skill> directory holding a SKILL.md is flattened into ~/.claude/skills/<skill>; each commands/<category>/<name> directory is copied to ~/.claude/commands/<category>-<name>; each subagents/core/<name>/agent.md is rewritten into a flat ~/.claude/agents/<name>.md with the frontmatter fields Claude Code does not support stripped; the whole subagents/ tree is copied to ~/.claude/subagents/; and prompts/, standards/, examples/, README.md, and CONTRIBUTING.md are copied to ~/.claude/tresor-resources/, which the script also names in the ~/.claude/tresor.config.json it writes. The README's manual path differs: it copies agents/ rather than subagents/core/ into ~/.claude/agents/, installs no subagents, and puts the reference documents in ~/claude-code-resources/ instead.
packs.distribution_machinery: scripts/install.sh checks for git, creates ~/.claude/{commands,agents,skills,templates}, copies an existing ~/.claude/ to a timestamped backup when a previous install is present, clones or pulls the repository into ~/.claude/tresor, copies the pack's documents to the destinations above, and writes ~/.claude/tresor.config.json; it takes --skills-only, --commands-only, --agents-only, --orchestration, --resources-only, --update, --backup-dir, and --no-backup. scripts/update.sh refreshes an existing install. commitlint.config.js is the repository's own commit tooling and is not installed.
packs.not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back and does no enforced work: everything installed is Markdown that Claude Code reads and executes with its own tools, and the only code it ships copies those files into the host's discovery directories.
packs.license_note: Repository-wide MIT license file, copyright 2025 Alireza Rezvani.

packs.name: Second Brain LLM Wiki
packs.description: Four Agent Skills documents a coding agent reads to scaffold, fill, query, and lint an Obsidian vault it maintains as an LLM-compiled wiki.
packs.installs: Four skill directories under skills/, each holding one SKILL.md: second-brain (an onboarding wizard), second-brain-ingest, second-brain-query, and second-brain-lint. The onboarding skill also bundles six reference documents under skills/second-brain/references/ (agent-config templates for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI, a tooling guide, and the wiki schema) and one script, scripts/onboarding.sh, with a shell test beside it under tests/. The README installs the whole pack with npx skills add NicholasSpisak/second-brain and names Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI as hosts, which are the four the agent-config templates cover; it also says 40+ other Agent Skills hosts work, which is a format compatibility list rather than a documented install and is not recorded. Two further documents, docs/llm-wiki.md and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, describe the pattern and are not installed into a host.
packs.distribution_machinery: skills/second-brain/scripts/onboarding.sh, which the onboarding skill tells the host to run once: it creates the vault's raw/, wiki/, and output/ directories, writes an empty wiki/index.md and wiki/log.md if they do not exist, reports whether three optional command-line tools are installed, and prints a JSON summary. It is idempotent scaffolding that reads nothing back and runs nothing at a later turn; tests/test_onboarding.sh exercises it.
packs.not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back and does no enforced work: the wiki, its index, and its operation log are written and re-read by the host agent following the skill documents, and the only shipped code scaffolds the vault once at setup. The published second-brain project record is a different system with the same repository name, separated under ADR 020 by its own SQLite-backed store, terminal, web, and API surfaces, and container execution, none of which this pack has.

packs.name: TypeSafe Agent Skills
packs.description: One Agent Skills document that tells a coding agent how to design and write software against TypeSafe's System One API, shipped with the Claude Code plugin and marketplace manifests that install it.
packs.installs: One skill directory, skills/typesafe-ai/, holding one SKILL.md and a copy of the licence. Two manifests under .claude-plugin/ wrap it for Claude Code: marketplace.json names one plugin, typesafe, whose source is the repository root, and plugin.json gives that plugin a version and declares no commands, agents, hooks, or servers, so Claude Code discovers the single skill from the skills/ folder and offers it as /typesafe:typesafe-ai. The README installs it with claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills followed by claude plugin install typesafe@typesafe-ai. It also gives npx skills add typesafe-ai/skills --skill typesafe-ai for other agents and says to select an agent when prompted; that names no host and documents no host-specific install, so only Claude Code is recorded. The skill's text points the agent at TypeSafe's live documentation index and cookbooks and describes the three question types and how to compose them; it carries no reference files of its own.
packs.distribution_machinery: None. The tree holds two JSON manifests, a README, one SKILL.md, and two copies of one licence file; there is no install script, hook, or other program.
packs.not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back and does no enforced work: the repository contains no code at all, and everything the skill causes is done by the host agent following one document. The TypeSafe API the document describes is a separate operational service with its own boundary, and the Jev 1.13 model behind it is a separate reviewed model record. This catalog's own maintenance scripts call that API, so the record rests only on the repository's tree and first-party install documentation.
